sentences.en: A few years after the Communist Revolution brought Mao Zedong to power,
sentences.zh: 在共产主义革命使毛泽东掌权几年后，

sentences.en: China's leader ordered his people to exterminate four pests.
sentences.zh: 中国领导人下令全国消灭四害。

sentences.en: Rats, flies, mosquitoes, and sparrows.
sentences.zh: 即老鼠、苍蝇、蚊子和麻雀。

sentences.en: The birds were eating China's grain.
sentences.zh: 当时鸟儿在啄食中国的粮食。

sentences.en: Chairman Mao had recently collectivized agriculture,
sentences.zh: 毛主席当时刚推行农业集体化，

sentences.en: and he wanted to kill off the birds consuming his country's food.
sentences.zh: 他想消灭那些消耗国家粮食的鸟类。

sentences.en: During the Great Sparrow Campaign, as the effort was called,
sentences.zh: 在被称为“打麻雀运动”的期间，

sentences.en: millions of birds were killed.
sentences.zh: 数以百万计的麻雀被杀死了。

sentences.en: People shot sparrows or banged on pots and pans
sentences.zh: 人们射杀麻雀，或者敲锣打鼓，

sentences.en: until the birds fell to the ground in exhaustion.
sentences.zh: 直到鸟儿因精疲力竭而坠地。

sentences.en: But the eradication of the sparrows produced an unintended consequence.
sentences.zh: 但消灭麻雀产生了一个意想不到的后果。

sentences.en: Insect populations soared because one of their natural predators had been eliminated.
sentences.zh: 由于其中一种天敌被消灭，昆虫数量激增。

sentences.en: Locusts swept across China's fields, decimating crops,
sentences.zh: 蝗虫席卷了中国的田野，摧毁了农作物，

sentences.en: and contributing to a great famine.
sentences.zh: 并导致了一场大饥荒。

sentences.en: Official figures put the death toll at 15 million people.
sentences.zh: 官方统计的死亡人数为1500万。

sentences.en: Unofficial numbers were two to five times higher.
sentences.zh: 非官方数据则高出两到五倍。

sentences.en: While the scale of the disaster was unimaginable,
sentences.zh: 虽然这场灾难的规模令人难以想象，

sentences.en: China is hardly alone when it comes to wrong-headed policies.
sentences.zh: 但在制定错误政策方面，中国绝非孤例。

sentences.en: From nations and governments to companies and families,
sentences.zh: 从国家和政府到公司和家庭，

sentences.en: humans regularly fail to foresee how initiatives can backfire.
sentences.zh: 人类经常无法预见举措会如何适得其反。

sentences.zh: 本周，我们继续“成功2.0”系列节目，

sentences.zh: 探讨我们生活中导致失败的主要根源之一。

sentences.zh: 其中一人将获得一百万美元的彩票奖金，这很棒。

sentences.en: You know, it's nice.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这挺好的。

sentences.en: What can go wrong?
sentences.zh: 能出什么问题呢？

sentences.en: So, here's a thought experiment.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有一个思想实验。

sentences.en: Imagine that someone invites you to join a test for a new drug.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，有人邀请你参加一种新药的测试。

sentences.en: They tell you that's, you know, a headache, a pill that you can take, and your headache will go away.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉你，这是一种治疗头痛的药片，你吃了头痛就会消失。

sentences.en: And there are no side effects that we know, and we'll pay you $50 for participating.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知没有副作用，而且我们会支付你50美元作为参与报酬。

sentences.en: That's basically what the FDA does in many cases, and I think that it makes sense to do.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是FDA在许多情况下所做的，我认为这样做是有道理的。

sentences.en: And I would be willing to take part in such a study.
sentences.zh: 我愿意参加这样的研究。

sentences.en: Now, imagine that it's the same, but they tell you we'll pay you $50,000 for participating.
sentences.zh: 现在，想象一下情况相同，但他们告诉你，我们会支付你5万美元作为参与报酬。

sentences.en: Now, I'll be worried, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，我会担心的，对吧？

sentences.en: If there are no side effects, why are they offering me so much money to take this one pill?
sentences.zh: 如果没有副作用，他们为什么要给我这么多钱让我吃这一片药？

sentences.en: And they think that this signaled that if you're paying me a million dollars to get vaccinated,
sentences.zh: 他们认为这传递了一个信号：如果你付我一百万美元让我接种疫苗，

sentences.en: it must be really bad for me to get vaccinated, right?
sentences.zh: 那接种疫苗一定真的很糟糕，对吧？

sentences.en: Because otherwise, why do you have to pay me to do it?
sentences.zh: 否则，你为什么要付钱让我去做呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Remember that we talked about completing the story.
sentences.zh: 记得我们谈过补全故事吗？

sentences.en: This completes the story in a different way than you intended.
sentences.zh: 这以一种不同于你预想的方式补全了故事。

sentences.en: You wanted to tell them, look, I care about you so much that I'm willing to pay you because it's so important,
sentences.zh: 你本想告诉他们，看，我非常关心你，所以我愿意付钱给你，因为这非常重要，

sentences.en: and the bad things that can happen are so bad that I want to encourage you.
sentences.zh: 而且可能发生的坏事太严重了，所以我想要鼓励你。

sentences.en: That was your story.
sentences.zh: 那是你的故事。

sentences.en: But the story that the people may hear is that this is actually bad for you.
sentences.zh: 但人们听到的故事可能是，这实际上对你不好。

sentences.en: It's so bad that we are willing to pay you a million dollars to do it.
sentences.zh: 它太糟糕了，以至于我们愿意付给你一百万美元让你去做。

sentences.en: Another dimension of incentives that makes them tricky has to do with the fact that the people we're trying to influence
sentences.zh: 激励机制的另一个维度使其变得棘手，这与我们试图影响的人有关，

sentences.en: perceive not just a carrot, but also a stick.
sentences.zh: 他们感知的不仅仅是胡萝卜，还有大棒。

sentences.en: So when people don't achieve an objective, they start to ask, what's going to happen if I fail?
sentences.zh: 所以当人们没有达到目标时，他们开始问，如果我失败了会发生什么？

sentences.en: Uri, tell me what happened at Wells Fargo Bank in the early 2000s when they introduced an incentive to increase performance.
sentences.zh: 尤里，告诉我21世纪初富国银行在引入提高绩效的激励措施时发生了什么。

sentences.en: So the CEO had a great idea.
sentences.zh: 首席执行官有个好主意。

sentences.en: I want every customer that we have to have at least eight products from the bank.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们拥有的每一位客户至少拥有银行的八种产品。

sentences.en: So if the customer has, say, a checking account, I want her to also have a credit card and saving account and whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以如果客户有一个支票账户，我也希望她有信用卡、储蓄账户等等。

sentences.en: And they gave very strong incentives for the people working in the bank to actually do that.
sentences.zh: 他们为银行员工提供了非常强力的激励措施来真正做到这一点。

sentences.en: And actually, if you did not meet the goals that they gave, it's not only that you didn't get the incentives,
sentences.zh: 实际上，如果你没有达到他们设定的目标，不仅得不到激励，

sentences.en: you were also very likely to be fired because your colleagues were able to do it.
sentences.zh: 你还很有可能被解雇，因为你的同事都能做到。

sentences.en: Now, it turns out that it's very hard to do it.
sentences.zh: 现在，事实证明这很难做到。

sentences.en: The way the colleagues were able to do it is by making up accounts.
sentences.zh: 同事们能够做到的方式是编造账户。

sentences.en: So, you know, think about the image of a worker coming to the bank in the morning, drinks his or her coffee,
sentences.zh: 所以，想象一下一个员工早上来到银行，喝着咖啡，

sentences.en: sit down at the computer and start making up fake accounts.
sentences.zh: 坐在电脑前开始编造虚假账户的画面。

sentences.en: According to authorities, inside Wells Fargo, employees called it gaming,
sentences.zh: 据当局称，在富国银行内部，员工称之为“博弈”，

sentences.en: forging customer signatures, creating pins to activate unauthorized debit cards,
sentences.zh: 伪造客户签名，创建密码以激活未经授权的借记卡，

sentences.en: and moving money to unauthorized accounts.
sentences.zh: 并将资金转移到未经授权的账户中。

sentences.en: I had 15 accounts at once.
sentences.zh: 我曾同时拥有15个账户。

sentences.en: It was just very frustrating.
sentences.zh: 这真是太令人沮丧了。

sentences.en: And these are accounts I never opened.
sentences.zh: 而这些都是我从未开过的账户。

sentences.en: And it wasn't one or two people.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是一两个人。

sentences.en: We're talking about over 3 million accounts.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是超过300万个账户。

sentences.en: And they fired at the end over 5,000 people for doing this.
sentences.zh: 最终他们因为这样做解雇了超过5000人。

sentences.en: So basically, the CEO wanted to have more products per account, got exactly what he wanted.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，首席执行官想要每个账户有更多的产品，他确实得到了他想要的。

sentences.en: The stock of Wells Fargo went up.
sentences.zh: 富国银行的股价上涨了。

sentences.en: Everything was fine, apart from the fact that it was all a balloon that was clearly going to explode at one point
sentences.zh: 一切都很好，除了这一切都是一个显然会在某个时刻爆炸的气球，

sentences.en: because it was all fake.
sentences.zh: 因为这一切都是假的。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if part of the problem here, Uri, is that the leaders were trying to incentivize
sentences.zh: 我在想，尤里，这里的部分问题是否在于领导者试图激励

sentences.en: an explicit behavior, which is to aggressively sell the company's products,
sentences.zh: 一种明确的行为，即积极销售公司的产品，

sentences.en: but they ignored how this incentive might affect other behaviors, including the implicit norm, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 但他们忽略了这种激励可能会如何影响其他行为，包括诚实的隐含规范。

sentences.en: They probably weren't thinking at the point they set up the incentive program.
sentences.zh: 他们在制定激励计划时可能并没有考虑这一点。

sentences.en: Well, what happens when people don't meet this target?
sentences.zh: 那么，当人们没有达到这个目标时会发生什么？

sentences.en: What are they going to do?
sentences.zh: 他们会怎么做？

sentences.en: So giving people incentives to create extra account is not bad in itself.
sentences.zh: 所以给人们激励去创建额外账户本身并不坏。

sentences.en: It will work.
sentences.zh: 这会奏效。

sentences.en: People will try harder.
sentences.zh: 人们会更加努力。

sentences.en: But at the same time, they have to put some safety measures that will make sure that people don't lie.
sentences.zh: 但同时，他们必须采取一些安全措施，确保人们不会撒谎。

sentences.en: So when you design incentives like this, think about how can people try and game the incentive?
sentences.zh: 所以当你设计这样的激励措施时，要考虑人们会如何尝试钻激励机制的空子？

sentences.en: Because that's what we do.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是我们所做的。

sentences.en: We game the incentives all the time.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在钻激励机制的空子。

sentences.en: We are very good at it.
sentences.zh: 我们非常擅长这一点。

sentences.en: We are very creative at it.
sentences.zh: 我们在这一点上非常有创造力。

sentences.en: So, for example, if there was enough auditing done, and once you catch someone making up an account,
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，如果进行了足够的审计，一旦你抓到有人编造账户，

sentences.en: you immediately fired that person, that would have worked.
sentences.zh: 你立即解雇那个人，那就会奏效。

sentences.en: But instead, what happened is that even whistleblower that came to management and said,
sentences.zh: 但相反，发生的情况是，即使是向管理层举报并说，

sentences.en: this is happening, they were actually fired.
sentences.zh: 这正在发生的人，实际上也被解雇了。

sentences.en: So the incentive in itself wasn't bad.
sentences.zh: 所以激励本身并不坏。

sentences.en: It just lacked the safety measure that was needed.
sentences.zh: 它只是缺乏所需的安全措施。

sentences.en: You cite a revealing incident from colonial era Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 你引用了殖民时代越南的一个发人深省的事件。

sentences.en: French authorities were confronting a problem, and they came up with a solution.
sentences.zh: 法国当局面临一个问题，他们想出了一个解决方案。

sentences.en: It involved incentivizing ordinary people to go out and kill rats.
sentences.zh: 它涉及激励普通人去捕杀老鼠。

sentences.en: But that incentive ended up producing a problem of its own.
sentences.zh: 但这种激励最终产生了它自己的问题。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened, Uri.
sentences.zh: 告诉我发生了什么，尤里。

sentences.en: So the French wanted to introduce toilets to Hanoi, which is very French of them to do.
sentences.zh: 法国人想在河内引入厕所，这非常符合他们的作风。

sentences.en: And when the toilets were introduced, you also need sewage.
sentences.zh: 当引入厕所时，你还需要污水处理系统。

sentences.en: And with sewage come the rats.
sentences.zh: 而污水处理系统带来了老鼠。

sentences.en: So there was a big problem with rats, and the authorities were very smart.
sentences.zh: 所以老鼠问题很严重，当局非常聪明。

sentences.en: They said, let's pay, say, 10 cents per rat tail that you bring.
sentences.zh: 他们说，让我们为每带回一条老鼠尾巴支付10美分。

sentences.en: So there was a poor guy in the city hall that was counting rats' tails.
sentences.zh: 市政厅里有个可怜的家伙在数老鼠尾巴。

sentences.en: And for each one of them, he gave 10 cents.
sentences.zh: 每带回一条，他就给10美分。

sentences.en: That sounds, again, like a very good incentive.
sentences.zh: 这听起来又是一个非常好的激励措施。

sentences.en: What can go wrong?
sentences.zh: 能出什么问题呢？

sentences.en: That's, you give the people, you let the people go after the rats, everything's going to be well.
sentences.zh: 这就是，你给人们，你让人们去追捕老鼠，一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: Well, it turns out, for example, that people just cut the tail of the rat and let the rat go free,
sentences.zh: 好吧，事实证明，例如，人们只是切下老鼠的尾巴，然后把老鼠放走，

sentences.en: because the rat can have more babies that way.
sentences.zh: 因为这样老鼠可以生更多的宝宝。

sentences.en: Some of them started their rat farMs.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至开始经营他们的“老鼠养殖场”。

sentences.en: So they started to raise their own rats in order to harvest their tails.
sentences.zh: 所以他们开始饲养自己的老鼠来收获它们的尾巴。

sentences.en: Some of them brought rats from neighboring cities in order to cut their tails.
sentences.zh: 有些人从邻近城市带老鼠来切它们的尾巴。

sentences.en: So, again, people are really good at gaming the incentives.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们真的很擅长钻激励机制的空子。

sentences.en: And you need to find a way and incentives that actually is robust to such manipulation.
sentences.zh: 你需要找到一种方法和激励措施，能够真正抵御这种操纵。

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting because I think this draws attention to the fact that when you're leading a company or a city or a country,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣，因为我认为这引起了人们的注意，当你领导一家公司、一个城市或一个国家时，

sentences.en: you know, it's very easy to focus on something that is not going well
sentences.zh: 你知道，很容易专注于某件进展不顺利的事情，

sentences.en: and come up with a simple plan to fix that thing.
sentences.zh: 并想出一个简单的计划来解决它。

sentences.en: But the problematic thing usually doesn't exist in a vacuum.
sentences.zh: 但问题通常不是孤立存在的。

sentences.en: It's connected to other things or it can influence things one layer beneath the surface.
sentences.zh: 它与其他事物相连，或者它可以影响表面之下的一层事物。

sentences.en: And in some ways, I think what all these examples are pointing to is the complexity of human behavior
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我认为所有这些例子都指向了人类行为的复杂性，

sentences.en: and perhaps how we need to exercise a certain amount of humility when it comes to trying to engineer that behavior.
sentences.zh: 以及在试图设计这种行为时，我们可能需要保持一定的谦逊。

sentences.en: So when I work with companies, very often I hear some version of, we tried incentives and they didn't work.
sentences.zh: 所以当我与公司合作时，我经常听到某种版本的说法：我们尝试了激励措施，但它们不起作用。

sentences.en: And when I hear this, I think about, you know, someone went to a bad Japanese restaurant
sentences.zh: 当我听到这个时，我想到了，你知道，有人去了一家糟糕的日本餐厅，

sentences.en: and his or her conclusion is, Japanese food is bad.
sentences.zh: 他或她的结论是，日本料理很糟糕。

sentences.en: No, that's not the right conclusion.
sentences.zh: 不，那不是正确的结论。

sentences.en: You went to a bad restaurant.
sentences.zh: 你只是去了一家糟糕的餐厅。

sentences.en: And the same is true about incentives.
sentences.zh: 激励措施也是如此。

sentences.en: It's not that incentives don't work.
sentences.zh: 并不是激励措施不起作用。

sentences.en: It's just that you didn't understand the complexity of incentives.
sentences.zh: 只是你没有理解激励措施的复杂性。

sentences.en: Incentives are powerful tools.
sentences.zh: 激励措施是强大的工具。

sentences.en: They can make people act in ways they would not have left to their own devices.
sentences.zh: 它们可以使人们以他们自己不会采取的方式行事。

sentences.en: But misunderstood or misapplied, incentives can backfire and boomerang.
sentences.zh: 但如果被误解或误用，激励措施可能会适得其反，产生回旋镖效应。

sentences.en: When we come back, how to craft incentives that get yourself and others moving in the direction of success.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将探讨如何制定激励措施，让你自己和他人朝着成功的方向前进。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Economist Uri Gneesi is the author of Mixed Signals, How Incentives Really Work.
sentences.zh: 经济学家尤里·格尼西是《混合信号：激励机制如何真正运作》一书的作者。

sentences.en: He studies the science of how we use carrots and sticks to get others to behave the way we want.
sentences.zh: 他研究我们如何利用胡萝卜加大棒来让别人按照我们想要的方式行事的科学。

sentences.en: Uri, when someone crafts an incentive, the people being incentivized use the signal of the incentive to draw conclusions about the sender.
sentences.zh: Uri，当有人设计一种激励措施时，被激励者会利用这种激励发出的信号来推断激励发起人的意图。

sentences.en: So poorly designed or poorly presented incentives can backfire by making the creator of the incentive look callous or greedy.
sentences.zh: 因此，设计糟糕或呈现方式不当的激励措施可能会适得其反，让发起人显得冷酷或贪婪。

sentences.en: You recently observed this in an initiative launched by a movie theater chain.
sentences.zh: 你最近在一家连锁电影院推出的举措中观察到了这一点。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what happened?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: So recently, AMC decided to have different prices for different seats.
sentences.zh: 最近，AMC 决定对不同的座位实行不同的定价。

sentences.en: They understood that people don't like to sit up front or on the sides.
sentences.zh: 他们明白人们不喜欢坐在前排或两侧。

sentences.en: And their solution was, let's raise the price for the middle seats, for the premium seat.
sentences.zh: 于是他们的解决方案是：提高中间座位，也就是黄金座位的价格。

sentences.en: And that's what airlines are doing.
sentences.zh: 航空公司也是这么做的。

sentences.en: That's what hotels are doing.
sentences.zh: 酒店也是这么做的。

sentences.en: But the way they did it really created a pushback.
sentences.zh: 但他们采取的方式确实引发了抵制。

sentences.en: Many people were upset.
sentences.zh: 很多人感到不满。

sentences.en: You know, the prices are already so high.
sentences.zh: 你知道，票价本来就已经很高了。

sentences.en: And now you're charging us more for the premium seats.
sentences.zh: 现在你们还要对黄金座位收取更高的费用。

sentences.en: That's really a nasty behavior.
sentences.zh: 这行为真的很恶劣。

sentences.en: That's the story that people heard.
sentences.zh: 这就是人们听到的故事版本。

sentences.en: But instead of that, AMC could have said, look, we're sorry.
sentences.zh: 但 AMC 本可以换种说法，比如：看，我们很抱歉。

sentences.en: Prices are so high.
sentences.zh: 价格太高了。

sentences.en: The inflation, whatever.
sentences.zh: 通货膨胀什么的。

sentences.en: We need to raise our prices.
sentences.zh: 我们需要涨价。

sentences.en: We're sorry.
sentences.zh: 我们很抱歉。

sentences.en: But here's the good news.
sentences.zh: 但有个好消息。

sentences.en: We're going to give you a discount if you're willing to sit in the first row or on the sides.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意坐在前排或两侧，我们将为你提供折扣。

sentences.en: So exactly the same incentives, but frame them.
sentences.zh: 所以激励措施完全一样，但要换个包装。

sentences.en: Tell the story.
sentences.zh: 讲好这个故事。

sentences.en: Fill up the story in a way that instead of I'm greedy and want to take even more money from you,
sentences.zh: 把故事编得圆满一点，而不是传达出“我很贪婪，想从你身上榨取更多钱”的意思，

sentences.en: is the story that you're telling is, look, we're trying to help you.
sentences.zh: 你传达的故事应该是：看，我们是在试图帮助你。

sentences.en: And we are offering this discount on less desirable seats.
sentences.zh: 我们正在为那些不太理想的座位提供折扣。

sentences.en: So in other words, let's say, for example, the ticket prices were $10.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，假设票价是 10 美元。

sentences.en: And you're charging $15 for the premium seats.
sentences.zh: 而你对黄金座位收取 15 美元。

sentences.en: What you're saying is, you know, raise the ticket prices to $15 for everyone and then basically make the less attractive seats discounted to $10.
sentences.zh: 你其实是在说：把所有人的票价都提高到 15 美元，然后基本上让那些不太吸引人的座位打折到 10 美元。

sentences.en: It comes to the same thing, but the story becomes completely different.
sentences.zh: 结果是一样的，但故事的性质完全变了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Instead of I'm taking advantage of you whenever I can, it's I'm trying to help you whenever I can.
sentences.zh: 与其表现得“我一有机会就占你便宜”，不如表现为“我一有机会就想帮助你”。

sentences.en: I had to raise prices because everything costs more.
sentences.zh: 我不得不涨价，因为什么都变贵了。

sentences.en: We have to pay more for our workforce.
sentences.zh: 我们必须支付更高的员工工资。

sentences.en: We have to pay more for rent.
sentences.zh: 我们必须支付更高的租金。

sentences.en: So we had to do this, but we really care about the people that have hard time paying, and we really want them to actually keep coming.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不得不这样做，但我们真的很关心那些支付困难的人，我们真心希望他们能继续来看电影。

sentences.en: So this points, of course, to the importance of paying attention not just to the incentive, but the story that the incentive is communicating.
sentences.zh: 所以，这当然指出了不仅要关注激励本身，还要关注激励所传达的故事的重要性。

sentences.en: Some companies have found a way to use incentives to tell a consistent story about their values.
sentences.zh: 一些公司已经找到了一种方法，利用激励措施来讲述一个关于其价值观的一致性故事。

sentences.en: And you say that one such company is the sandwich chain, Pret a Manger.
sentences.zh: 你说其中一家公司就是三明治连锁店 Pret a Manger。

sentences.en: How did they design incentives, Uri?
sentences.zh: Uri，他们是如何设计激励措施的？

sentences.en: So they wanted to give some kind of bonus, like employee of the week or something like that, and give you a bonus.
sentences.zh: 他们想发放某种奖金，比如“周度员工”之类的，给你发奖金。

sentences.en: Now, in every case that you're doing something like this, you're actually doing something else as well.
sentences.zh: 现在，在你做这类事情的每一种情况下，你实际上也在做另一件事。

sentences.en: You're also, it's not just the people that you invite to the party, it's also the people that you don't invite that you should care about.
sentences.zh: 你不仅要考虑那些被邀请参加派对的人，还应该关心那些没被邀请的人。

sentences.en: So the people that in this case did not get the bonus, in this case the bonus was $50.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这个案例中没有得到奖金的人——这次奖金是 50 美元——

sentences.en: And the way they thought to reduce the problem was that if you were the employee of the week or of the month, you got the $50, but you were asked to spend it on someone else,
sentences.zh: 他们想出的减少问题的方法是：如果你是周度或月度优秀员工，你得到了这 50 美元，但你被要求把它花在别人身上，

sentences.en: on one of your friends.
sentences.zh: 花在你的朋友之一身上。

sentences.en: So the incentive on the surface is designed to reward people for reaching a milestone, but really the way the company is using it,
sentences.zh: 所以，表面上的激励是为了奖励达到里程碑的人，但实际上公司使用它的方式是，

sentences.en: the incentive is designed to enhance team building.
sentences.zh: 这种激励旨在加强团队建设。

sentences.en: Yes, if it's a subjective measure, for example, how well you did on something that we can't measure in dollars,
sentences.zh: 是的，如果这是一个主观的衡量标准，例如，你在某些我们无法用金钱衡量的事情上做得有多好，

sentences.en: then I'm going to be upset if you'll get the reward because I'm clearly better than you.
sentences.zh: 那么如果你得到了奖励，我会很不高兴，因为我显然比你做得更好。

sentences.en: This way, it reduced by a lot the tension between the employees about who's going to win this.
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，它极大地减少了员工之间关于谁会获胜的紧张关系。

sentences.en: So winning it was, you still got you the status and it was nice, you felt good about yourself, but the money you gave to other people.
sentences.zh: 所以获胜依然能让你获得地位，感觉很好，你对自己感觉良好，但钱是你给别人的。

sentences.en: So other people, the workers became more friendly with each other and there was less tension over there.
sentences.zh: 因此，其他人，员工们彼此变得更加友好，那里的紧张气氛也减少了。

sentences.en: One problem with incentives is that people will change their behavior for as long as they're being incentivized to do so,
sentences.zh: 激励措施的一个问题是，人们只会在受到激励的情况下改变行为，

sentences.en: but will then revert to their previous behavior once the incentive is withdrawn.
sentences.zh: 但一旦激励撤销，他们就会恢复到之前的行为。

sentences.en: Your own research, however, has shown that incentives can create long-lasting change if they are used in a particular way.
sentences.zh: 然而，你自己的研究表明，如果以特定的方式使用，激励措施可以产生持久的改变。

sentences.en: Tell us about your study about building exercise habits, Uri.
sentences.zh: 跟我们讲讲你关于建立锻炼习惯的研究吧，Uri。

sentences.en: So creating habits is maybe the holy grail of incentives.
sentences.zh: 所以，养成习惯也许是激励机制的圣杯。

sentences.en: How can we change your habits?
sentences.zh: 我们如何改变你的习惯？

sentences.en: How can we get you to exercise more, stop smoking or diet better, whatever is the activity that you want to do?
sentences.zh: 我们如何让你多锻炼、戒烟或更好地节食，无论你想做什么活动？

sentences.en: It turns out to be very difficult because it's an ongoing behavior which is very hard to change.
sentences.zh: 事实证明这非常困难，因为这是一种持续的行为，很难改变。

sentences.en: And many of us, those of us that struggle with this, including me, remember periods of their life in which they exercised.
sentences.zh: 我们中的许多人，包括我在内，在与此斗争时，都会想起生命中曾经锻炼过的那段时期。

sentences.en: So there were periods in my life in which I exercised that I was very happy about is going to the gym or surfing or biking, whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 我生命中确实有过锻炼的时期，那时我很高兴去健身房、冲浪或骑自行车，无论是什么运动。

sentences.en: And then I have periods in my life in which I can't get myself off the couch.
sentences.zh: 然后我生命中又会有一些时期，我根本无法让自己离开沙发。

sentences.en: The only physical activity is watching Netflix.
sentences.zh: 唯一的体力活动就是看 Netflix。

sentences.en: What's the difference between these two?
sentences.zh: 这两者之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: And what we thought about, and there is some literature suggesting this, that once you get into the activity, so say for a month, after that, it's much easier.
sentences.zh: 我们所想的是——也有一些文献支持这一点——一旦你进入了这种活动，比如坚持了一个月，之后就容易多了。

sentences.en: So the first time you go to the gym, it smells bad, you don't know where to park, you don't know what to do, it's kind of embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 所以你第一次去健身房时，那里味道不好，你不知道在哪停车，不知道该做什么，有点尴尬。

sentences.en: After a month, suddenly you don't bother the smell that much, and you know exactly what you're going to do.
sentences.zh: 一个月后，突然间你就不那么在意气味了，而且你确切地知道自己要做什么。

sentences.en: And say you put it in your schedule that Monday and Thursday at 9 a.m.
sentences.zh: 假设你把它排进了日程表，周一和周四早上 9 点，

sentences.en: I'm going to do yoga classes, whatever it is that you're doing.
sentences.zh: 我要去上瑜伽课，或者无论你在做什么。

sentences.en: Suddenly it becomes much easier for you.
sentences.zh: 突然间，这对你来说就容易多了。

sentences.en: And the idea was that if you can build this, if you can invest in this month, even if you're going to suffer and you think that the suffering is bigger than the benefit,
sentences.zh: 我们的想法是，如果你能建立这个习惯，如果你能投入这一个月，即使你会受苦，即使你认为痛苦大于收益，

sentences.en: just invest in this month, and then after that it might become really easier.
sentences.zh: 只要投入这一个月，之后它可能真的会变得容易得多。

sentences.en: So we did it with incentives.
sentences.zh: 所以我们用激励措施做了实验。

sentences.en: It was Gary Charnas and I.
sentences.zh: 那是 Gary Charnas 和我做的。

sentences.en: So we pay students $100 to go to the gym eight times for a month.
sentences.zh: 我们付给学生 100 美元，让他们一个月内去健身房八次。

sentences.en: And then after that, we stopped paying them.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，我们停止了支付。

sentences.en: And we saw that the people that got paid to go to the gym were much more likely to go to the gym than the control group.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，那些被付钱去健身房的人比对照组更有可能继续去健身房。

sentences.en: So we did create some kind of habit.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实养成了一种习惯。

sentences.en: Turns out that this habit dies quite faSt.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这种习惯消失得相当快。

sentences.en: So, you know, winter break, they come back, the habit is dead.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，寒假一过，他们回来，习惯就没了。

sentences.en: So how to maintain this habit is still a question.
sentences.zh: 所以如何维持这种习惯仍然是一个问题。

sentences.en: But it is interesting that if I can get you over this hurdle of actually going to the gym for a few times, it's going to be easier.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，如果我能让你克服去健身房几次的障碍，事情就会变得更容易。

sentences.en: Now, you can also think about it for yourself.
sentences.zh: 现在，你也可以为自己考虑一下。

sentences.en: You can incentivize yourself.
sentences.zh: 你可以激励自己。

sentences.en: The first time you'll go, like we said, you're going to suffer, but you should commit.
sentences.zh: 就像我们说的，第一次去你会受苦，但你应该做出承诺。

sentences.en: I'm going to force myself to go for a month, and only then I'm going to evaluate whether I want to continue.
sentences.zh: 我要强迫自己坚持一个月，然后才评估我是否想继续。

sentences.en: And you might be surprised by the outcome.
sentences.zh: 结果可能会让你感到惊讶。

sentences.en: A related idea is that incentives can also be used to help people get past what you call switching costs.
sentences.zh: 一个相关的观点是，激励措施也可以用来帮助人们克服你所说的“转换成本”。

sentences.en: What are these, Yuri?
sentences.zh: 那是什么，Uri？

sentences.en: So switching costs is something that we do all the time.
sentences.zh: 转换成本是我们一直在做的事情。

sentences.en: So we have this, imagine going to the supermarket.
sentences.zh: 想象一下去超市。

sentences.en: You know which kind of shampoo you're going to buy or toilet paper.
sentences.zh: 你知道你要买哪种洗发水或卫生纸。

sentences.en: Maybe at the beginning you searched a bit, but then you chose one brand of toilet papers, and that's what you're taking.
sentences.zh: 也许刚开始你搜索了一下，但后来你选择了一个品牌的卫生纸，这就是你一直买的。

sentences.en: Switching to another one will require standing over there, thinking about it, comparing prices.
sentences.zh: 换成另一种需要站在那里，思考它，比较价格。

sentences.en: Is it soft enough or not?
sentences.zh: 它够不够软？

sentences.en: You're not going to do it.
sentences.zh: 你不会去做的。

sentences.en: You're going to stay with the toilet paper that you know.
sentences.zh: 你会坚持用你熟悉的卫生纸。

sentences.en: Now imagine that you go, you reach to your regular toilet paper, and you see that the competitor is, as a discount, you know, half price, say.
sentences.zh: 现在想象一下，你走过去，拿到你常用的卫生纸，发现竞争对手的产品在打折，你知道，半价，比如说。

sentences.en: Now you're saying, wow, that's a big discount.
sentences.zh: 现在你会说，哇，这折扣很大。

sentences.en: Let me try the other one.
sentences.zh: 让我试试另一种吧。

sentences.en: I'll try it.
sentences.zh: 我会试一试。

sentences.en: You'll take it, try it, and if you like it, you might switch to it, and when you go back, you'll actually search for it because you'll like it,
sentences.zh: 你会拿走它，试用它，如果你喜欢它，你可能会换成它，当你回去时，你实际上会主动寻找它，因为你喜欢它，

sentences.en: even if there won't be a discount on it.
sentences.zh: 即使它没有折扣。

sentences.en: So there is a switching cost, which is, it could be a mental switching cost like that, that you just don't want to think about it.
sentences.zh: 所以存在一种转换成本，这可能是一种心理上的转换成本，就是你根本不想去想它。

sentences.en: There could be some other switching cost, like imagine now smoking, for example.
sentences.zh: 可能还有其他转换成本，比如现在想象一下吸烟。

sentences.en: Imagine that I can actually pay you to stop smoking for a month.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，我真的可以付钱让你戒烟一个月。

sentences.en: Maybe after a month, it's going to be less attractive for you to go back, and that's the idea, right?
sentences.zh: 也许一个月后，再回去吸烟对你来说就没那么有吸引力了，这就是这个想法，对吧？

sentences.en: So switching from one activity to another is costly.
sentences.zh: 所以从一种活动转换到另一种活动是有成本的。

sentences.en: If I'll give you a discount, if I'll give you incentives, I might get you to change your behavior in a way that you wouldn't do after that, and if I'm lucky,
sentences.zh: 如果我给你折扣，如果我给你激励，我可能会让你以一种你之后不会做的方式改变行为，如果我幸运的话，

sentences.en: you'll stick with the new behavior later on.
sentences.zh: 你以后会坚持这种新行为。

sentences.en: In many parts of our lives, we don't see the consequences of our actions until much later.
sentences.zh: 在我们生活的许多方面，直到很久以后我们才能看到自己行为的后果。

sentences.en: So if you start smoking, for example, it can take years or even decades before you pay the price in terms of health effects.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你开始吸烟，可能需要几年甚至几十年才能在健康影响方面付出代价。

sentences.en: The same thing goes for schooling, but in the opposite direction.
sentences.zh: 上学也是一样，但方向相反。

sentences.en: It often takes years before you can see the benefits of studying hard and doing well at school.
sentences.zh: 通常需要几年时间才能看到努力学习和在学校表现良好的好处。

sentences.en: You and others have done a lot of thinking about this problem and how incentives might be used to try and improve the performance of students in school.
sentences.zh: 你和其他人对这个问题进行了很多思考，以及如何利用激励措施来尝试提高学生在学校的表现。

sentences.en: Tell me about this work, Uri.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲这项工作吧，Uri。

sentences.en: So as a university professor, my life is quite boring.
sentences.zh: 作为一名大学教授，我的生活相当无聊。

sentences.en: You know, I don't get that many people mad at me unless I go and talk about incentives with educators.
sentences.zh: 你知道，除非我去和教育工作者谈论激励措施，否则没多少人会对我生气。

sentences.en: That's, you know, they want to kill me.
sentences.zh: 那是，你知道，他们想杀了我。

sentences.en: They want to choke me very faSt.
sentences.zh: 他们想很快地掐死我。

sentences.en: And I think that they are right in many cases because you want the students to have intrinsic motivation to be successful.
sentences.zh: 我认为在很多情况下他们是对的，因为你希望学生有内在动力去取得成功。

sentences.en: You don't want to pay the money in order to read books.
sentences.zh: 你不想为了让他们读书而付钱。

sentences.en: And we know that I can pay you money to read a book.
sentences.zh: 我们知道我可以付钱让你读一本书。

sentences.en: I can't pay you to start enjoying reading the books.
sentences.zh: 但我无法付钱让你开始享受读书的过程。

sentences.en: So it's much harder.
sentences.zh: 所以这难得多。

sentences.en: And they sympathize with the teachers and educators that say this.
sentences.zh: 我同情那些这么说的老师和教育工作者。

sentences.en: However, there are things that you can actually use in education that will be useful.
sentences.zh: 然而，在教育中确实有一些东西是可以利用的，而且是有用的。

sentences.en: So imagine my example is I, you know, I write a lot for my living.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下，我的例子是，你知道，我靠写作谋生。

sentences.en: And yet I write, you know, one finger at a time.
sentences.zh: 然而我写作时，你知道，一次只用一根手指。

sentences.en: I don't know how to type.
sentences.zh: 我不知道怎么打字。

sentences.en: If someone would have paid me enough money or convinced me to invest a week in learning touch typing, that would have been amazing for me.
sentences.zh: 如果有人付给我足够的钱或者说服我投入一周时间学习盲打，那对我来说太棒了。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: So once you learn a skill, you're not going to go back.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你学会了一项技能，你就不会再回去了。

sentences.en: And in education, you can think about some landmarks like this that are important.
sentences.zh: 在教育中，你可以考虑一些像这样的重要里程碑。

sentences.en: Imagine your annoying teenager and the SAT.
sentences.zh: 想象一下你那烦人的青少年孩子和 SAT 考试。

sentences.en: You understand how important it is.
sentences.zh: 你明白这有多重要。

sentences.en: You really want your kid to be successful.
sentences.zh: 你真的希望你的孩子成功。

sentences.en: But they have other things in mind.
sentences.zh: 但他们心里有别的事。

sentences.en: If you can find incentives to make sure that they actually prepare well for the SAT,
sentences.zh: 如果你能找到激励措施来确保他们确实为 SAT 做了充分准备，

sentences.en: that could still work.
sentences.zh: 那仍然可能奏效。

sentences.en: The bigger problem, which in which I agree with the teachers and the educator,
sentences.zh: 更大的问题，也就是我同意老师和教育工作者观点的地方，

sentences.en: is that you cannot use it in order to get kids, students to enjoy what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 是你不能用它来让孩子们、学生们享受他们正在做的事情。

sentences.en: That we don't know how to do.
sentences.zh: 那是我们不知道该怎么做的。

sentences.en: And that's much harder.
sentences.zh: 而且那要难得多。

sentences.en: At the same time, you know, it seems like I think the picture you're painting here is that incentives are perhaps potentially useful in sort of these narrow circumstances where,
sentences.zh: 同时，你知道，看起来我想你在这里描绘的图景是，激励措施在这些狭窄的情况下可能是有用的，

sentences.en: you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: the student basically is unable to really comprehend how, you know, applying himself or herself in school can pay off 20 or 30 years down the road.
sentences.zh: 学生们基本上无法真正理解，你知道，在学校里努力学习如何在20或30年后带来回报。

sentences.en: But a carefully targeted incentive can prompt the student to do better on a standardized test, for example, you know, a three-week sprint, for example.
sentences.zh: 但一个精心设计的激励措施可以促使学生在标准化考试中表现得更好，比如，你知道，一个为期三周的冲刺。

sentences.en: And that might, in fact, have long-term consequences that are beneficial.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上可能会产生有益的长期后果。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But I wouldn't be that pessimistic about the first part, because if you use the right incentives, you can make you actually studying more enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 但我不会对第一部分那么悲观，因为如果你使用正确的激励措施，你可以让学习变得更有趣。

sentences.en: We have a recent paper in which we looked at the effect of physical activity on success, academic success.
sentences.zh: 我们最近有一篇论文，研究了体育活动对成功，即学业成功的影响。

sentences.en: So imagine that all you care about is the math success, success in math for the kids.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下，你唯一关心的是数学成绩，孩子们在数学上的成功。

sentences.en: And currently they get 10 hours of math and two hours of physical education every week.
sentences.zh: 目前他们每周有10小时数学课和2小时体育课。

sentences.en: Now you have to cut two hours.
sentences.zh: 现在你必须削减2小时。

sentences.en: Which one should you cut?
sentences.zh: 你应该削减哪一个？

sentences.en: Should you cut down the two PE classes like most schools do?
sentences.zh: 你应该像大多数学校那样削减那两节体育课吗？

sentences.en: Or maybe two hours of the math, even if all you care about is math performance?
sentences.zh: 还是说，即使你只关心数学成绩，也应该削减两小时数学课？

sentences.en: It could be, and that's what we find.
sentences.zh: 有可能，而这正是我们的发现。

sentences.en: We find that students that are engaged in physical activity are actually doing much better academically.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，参与体育活动的学生实际上在学业上表现得更好。

sentences.en: So it might be better to take the two hours for math, let them run around, and go back.
sentences.zh: 所以，把两小时数学课拿出来，让他们跑一跑，然后再回来，这可能更好。

sentences.en: And this could be used also as incentives, right?
sentences.zh: 而且这也可以作为激励手段，对吧？

sentences.en: So if I tell you, look, finish up the work and you can go out and play some basketball, that could be used as incentive.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我告诉你，听着，把工作做完，你就可以出去打会儿篮球，这就可以作为激励。

sentences.en: And that's why the entire culture of politics is not, look, I'm good because I know how to run experiments
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么整个政治文化不是说：看，我很棒，因为我知道如何进行实验，

sentences.en: and find out what's the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 并找出什么是正确的做法。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: I want a politician that knows what's the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 我想要的是一位知道什么是正确做法的政治家。

sentences.en: And I think that that's a mistake.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这是一个错误。

sentences.zh: 尤里·格尼西是加州大学圣地亚哥分校的经济学家。

sentences.zh: 尤里，感谢你今天参加《Hidden Brain》节目。

sentences.en: For today's Unsung Hero, we bring you a story from our sister show, My Unsung Hero.
sentences.zh: 今天的“无名英雄”环节，我们为你带来姐妹节目《My Unsung Hero》中的一个故事。

sentences.en: The story comes from Sarah Feldman.
sentences.zh: 这个故事来自莎拉·费尔德曼。

sentences.en: In 2001, my hometown of Houston was hit by a tropical storm, and I was on vacation in Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 2001年，我的家乡休斯顿遭遇了一场热带风暴，当时我正在康涅狄格州度假。

sentences.en: We couldn't go home that day, of course, so my father decided to take me to the Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library in Yale University.
sentences.zh: 当然，那天我们回不了家，所以我父亲决定带我去耶鲁大学的拜内克古籍善本图书馆。

sentences.en: I was around 13 or 14 years old, and I was asking this gentleman named Bill Carver a bunch of questions like, how do you keep all these rare books okay,
sentences.zh: 那时我大约13或14岁，我问了一位名叫比尔·卡弗的先生一堆问题，比如：你是如何保护这些珍贵书籍的？

sentences.en: and what's the oldest book you have?
sentences.zh: 你们这里最古老的书是什么？

sentences.en: And then I told him about how my grandparents went into my house that was flooded, and all of my books, lots of them, because I was a big reader as a child, were destroyed.
sentences.zh: 然后我告诉他，我的祖父母去了我那被洪水淹没的房子，我小时候是个书迷，所以我的很多书都被毁了。

sentences.en: And he said to me, Sarah, I'm going to send you a book in the mail, so you can start your collection again.
sentences.zh: 他对我说：莎拉，我会寄一本书给你，这样你就可以重新开始你的收藏了。

sentences.en: And he did.
sentences.zh: 他真的这么做了。

sentences.en: And I got a really nice book called The Medieval Book by Barbara A.
sentences.zh: 我收到了一本非常精美的书，叫《中世纪之书》，作者是芭芭拉·A·

sentences.en: Shaler, and I also received a letter in the mail, and I'd like to read it to you.
sentences.zh: 沙勒。我还收到了一封信，我想读给你听。

sentences.en: December 8th, 2001, Dear Sarah, I have often thought of you and your family and that terrible flood of 2000.
sentences.zh: 2001年12月8日，亲爱的莎拉，我经常想起你和你的家人，以及2000年那场可怕的洪水。

sentences.en: He meant 2001.
sentences.zh: 他指的是2001年。

sentences.en: As promised, enclosed is a rather scholarly book, which you may be slightly mature for your age, but I thought it might help you shape your new library collection.
sentences.zh: 如约寄上这本相当学术的书，虽然对你的年龄来说可能稍微深奥了一些，但我认为它或许能帮助你构建新的藏书系列。

sentences.en: And as the years progress, this book may grow in stature and value to you.
sentences.zh: 随着岁月的流逝，这本书对你的意义和价值可能会与日俱增。

sentences.en: Have a happy holiday season.
sentences.zh: 祝你节日快乐。

sentences.en: Wish you and loved ones all the beSt.
sentences.zh: 祝你和你的亲人一切安好。

sentences.en: Cordially, Bill Carver.
sentences.zh: 诚挚的，比尔·卡弗。

sentences.en: I want to tell him that I'm 34 now, and my life is great.
sentences.zh: 我想告诉他，我现在34岁了，生活得很幸福。

sentences.en: I'm married, I have a dog, and my partner and I like to visit cathedrals in Europe and go to the Cloisters Museum in New York City from time to time,
sentences.zh: 我结婚了，养了一只狗，我和伴侣喜欢去欧洲参观大教堂，偶尔也会去纽约市的修道院博物馆，

sentences.en: and I'm obsessed with medieval art.
sentences.zh: 而且我痴迷于中世纪艺术。

sentences.en: I actually sent the library a letter during the pandemic, but I never heard back.
sentences.zh: 疫情期间我其实给图书馆写过一封信，但一直没收到回音。

sentences.en: I'm not sure if he's alive still because he seemed old to me when I was 14 at the time.
sentences.zh: 我不确定他是否还健在，因为我14岁那年见到他时，他看起来已经很老了。

sentences.en: But I'd just love to tell Bill Carver that he changed my life.
sentences.zh: 但我真的很想告诉比尔·卡弗，他改变了我的人生。

sentences.en: Sarah Feldman lives in New York City, where she has her own jewelry business.
sentences.zh: 莎拉·费尔德曼住在纽约市，她经营着自己的珠宝生意。

sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢今天的节目，请务必分享给几位朋友。

sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.zh: 再见。
